title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: NOURISH (Nature-Based Opportunities Underpinning Resilient and Sustainable Households) aims to reduce poverty and hunger in vulnerable households and communities in the Makira- Ulawa Province, Solomon Islands. The project aims to benefit 1,719 women, men, girls and boys through improved sustainable livelihoods, through nutrition sensitive climate smart approaches; increased consumption of nutritious and safe diets; strengthened Disaster Risk Reduction strategies with appropriate climate mitigation and adaptation activities and increased social and cultural empowerment for women and girls. NOURISH targets the poorest households, prioritising those that are female headed, or have a pregnant woman or young child, or are led by a person with a disability. Key activities include Climate Smart Agriculture; savings groups and microfinance; promoting household nutrition; prevention of post-harvest losses; disaster preparedness and management; social accountability around protection of the environment; natural resource management and climate adaptation; addressing harmful attitudes, norms, values and practices around gender equity and social inclusion.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Strengthened Disaster Risk Reduction and management strategies with appropriate climate mitigation and adaptation activities in target communities. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: NOURISH supports disaster risk reduction activities including risk assessments and preparedness measures (e.g. early warning systems), as well as building local and national capacities and supporting the establishment of efficient and sustainable national structures able to promote disaster risk reduction in the Makira- Ulawa Province, Solomon Islands.The principle aim of this objective is reduce the vulnerability to climate change impacts by strengthening systemic capacity in disaster response and management in target communities, increasing their ability to adapt to, or absorb, climate change stresses, shocks and variability and/or by helping reduce exposure to them.
